correctness.rationale: For unit x,y define C=∫x³y, E=∫xy³, D=∫x²y² and F=C−E. The pointwise polynomial identity ||x²−y²+√2xy||₂²=2+2√2F proves the sharp F≥−1/√2. The exact real quartic expansions and uniformly bounded fourth-root Taylor remainders give (||x+τy||₄+||τx−y||₄)/2=1+τF/2+τ²B+O(τ³), B=3D/2−3(C²+E²)/4. The identities for <R,xy> and <R,x²+y²> imply |B−9/16|≤4||R||₂. Completing the nonnegative defect quadratic gives the uniform lower 1−τ/(2√2)+9τ²/16−Kτ³ for all real L4 and any outer t≥1, using power-mean dominance over the arithmetic mean. On any two disjoint normalized supports, take x=af+bg,y=−bf+ag with a²=(√3+1)/(2√2),b²=(√3−1)/(2√2); both outputs have the identical fourth power 1−√2τ+3τ²+√2τ³+τ⁴, giving the uniform upper bound for every outer exponent including infinity. Equality in the square yields exactly two ratio levels r± and the specified y⁴-mass fractions. For O(τ³) near-optimal pairs the uncompleted quadratic forces ||R||₂=O(τ). Remainders are uniform via |C|,|E|,D≤1, τ≤1/8, and two-point power-mean comparison; no finite sampling substitutes for the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The skew Schäffer infimum is a natural published Banach-space geometric invariant, and the cross-exponent regime 1<=t<4 is a specific mathematical gap after the matching-exponent theorem. Determining its dimension-free sharp two-term onset, including t=1, is not a relabeling of the t=4 formula: prior monotonicity has the incorrect direction for the essential lower bound. A sharp square identity, two-level classification of antisymmetric duality-map extremizers, and quantitative O(τ) stability for O(τ³) almost-minimizers give structurally useful information about this non-Hilbert geometry. The object and invariant are intrinsically motivated independently of any speculative application; no general/downstream theorem is needed for mathematical value.
residual_risks: The exact deficit identity is elementary algebra by itself; assessed value rests on its nontrivial coupling to the sharp uniform local lower bound and rigidity.
No quantitative numerical-conditioning, algorithmic, or complex-space applications are claimed.

final_claim: In every real L4 space of dimension at least two, uniformly for 1<=t<=infinity, S_(X,t)(tau)=1-tau/(2sqrt(2))+9tau²/16+O(tau³) as tau downarrow zero, with absolute tau0,K. For any two unit x,y, ||x²-y²+sqrt(2)xy||₂²=2+2sqrt(2)∫xy(x²-y²); the latter integral has sharp infimum -1/sqrt(2), equality exactly at two permitted pointwise ratios (-sqrt(2)±sqrt(6))/2 with corresponding y⁴ masses (2±sqrt(3))/4. O(tau³)-almost-minimizing pairs for any t(tau) obey ||x²-y²+sqrt(2)xy||₂=O(tau).
limitations: Real L4, dimension >=2, local tau downarrow zero, t in [1,infinity]; no complex extension or global-tau minimizers.
